newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Style-conscious Argentina sees surge of anorexia.
newsitem.headline: Style-conscious Argentina sees surge of anorexia.

text.p: Anorexia and bulimia rates are surging in fashion-conscious Argentina, where a "narcissistic" culture is leading to alarmingly high death rates from eating disorders, an official report said on Friday.

"According to recent studies, one out of every 10 teenagers in Argentina is bulimic or anorexic, triple the rate of the United States. And nine out of 10 are women," the report by the National Women's Council said.
Buenos Aires, a city with a strong European flavor, is the fashion hub of Latin America and prides itself on style.

But Argentina's "narcissistic culture" is taking its toll on young girls with a mortality rate of 10 percent among victims of serious eating disorders, according to the report drawn up by the National Women's Council.
More and more women are turning up in doctor's offices.
"There is a strong rise in cases of consultation, especially for bulimia ... and a gradual drop in the age of victims," the report said.
The report blames the country's "narcissistic or 'barbie-doll' culture" for imposing impossible standards of beauty on adolescent girls.

"Dolls used to have the face of little girls; now they look like a miniature version of (supermodel) Claudia Schiffer," said Enrique Valiente, organizer of the Council's first national seminar on bulimia and anorexia last year.

"The barbie doll is an example of the prevailing cultural model, and it's very revealing because it must be almost 37 years old but it's looking younger than ever," he said, noting that the doll's comparative physical dimensions would be impossible for a human to achieve.
The Council said it would seek to encourage a public debate and national policies aimed at altering advertising bias and fashion designs so as to include women of all sizes.

"We must promote the inclusion of a wide range of female models in advertising and promote a healthy diet not tied to physical beauty standards," the council said. It urged women to "adopt a critical attitude and reject all actions that tend to disqualify their bodies."
